advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In the recording fake, snapshot the effective child env (`kwargs.get("env") or dict(os.environ)`) so the 'no other git call receives the header' test sees what inheriting children actually get
evidence: tests/unit/test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py:64: `calls.append({"cmd": [str(part) for part in cmd], "env": kwargs.get("env")})` records None for every call that inherits the parent environment

src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:358: `env = dict(os.environ)` is the copy this test is meant to guard; the checkout, remote-add and tickets fetch at gerrit_client.py:405-442 pass no env= and inherit os.environ
advisory.finding: test_no_other_git_call_receives_the_gerrit_header cannot detect the header leaking into later git calls through os.environ. Calls without an explicit env inherit os.environ, but the test replaces env=None with {} and asserts nothing about what those children actually inherit. If _gerrit_git_env wrote into os.environ instead of a copy (for example `env = os.environ` in place of `env = dict(os.environ)`), the checkout, remote-add and GitHub tickets fetch would all inherit the Authorization entry and this test would still pass.
scenarios: Someone refactors _gerrit_git_env to set the GIT_CONFIG_* variables on os.environ. Every later git child, including the GitHub tickets fetch, inherits the Gerrit Authorization config, and the test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _record_clone's _fake_run, record `"env": kwargs.get("env") if kwargs.get("env") is not None else dict(os.environ)`. Optionally also assert after the clone that no GIT_CONFIG_KEY_* in os.environ contains 'extraHeader'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the src/rebar credential scan catch multi-line argv lists (match over whole file text, or join adjacent lines), add a multi-line case to the pattern self-test, and assert that a non-zero number of files was scanned
evidence: tests/unit/test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py:165: `_ARGV_HEADER = re.compile(r"""["']-c["']\s*,\s*f?["'][^"']*(?:extraheader|authorization)""", re.I)` requires `-c` and the header value on the same line
src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:386-397 shows the house style: each argv element (`"git",`, `"-C",`, `*stall_abort_args(),`) on its own line
tests/unit/test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py:168-173: the pattern self-test uses only single-line inputs
tests/unit/test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py:182: `assert not hits` with no assertion that rglob found any files
advisory.finding: The static source guard checks one line at a time, so it misses an auth header passed as `-c` in a black-formatted, one-element-per-line argv list. That is the layout this module already uses for its git calls. The guard is a source grep, and it also never checks that any files were scanned, so its absence assertion passes trivially if the glob matches nothing.
scenarios: A future change adds `"-c",` on one line and `f"http.extraHeader=Authorization: {self._auth}",` on the next inside a subprocess.run list. Neither line matches _ARGV_HEADER, so the guard passes while the credential is back in argv.
The test runs from a layout where `parents[2]/src/rebar` does not exist or holds no .py files. The loop scans nothing and `assert not hits` passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Run the patterns over `path.read_text()` with `\s*` spanning newlines (e.g. `re.compile(r"[\"']-c[\"']\s*,\s*f?[\"'][^\"']*(?:extraheader|authorization)", re.I)` applied to the full text, then map match.start() back to a line number). Add a black-formatted multi-line case to test_the_patterns_flag_the_shapes_they_exist_to_catch, and add `assert files_scanned > 0` before `assert not hits`.
